speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in the recent layoffs by large tech companies (a) what is the number of employees retrenched; (b) what is the number of Singaporeans retrenched; and (c) what are the roles that have been impacted.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members have filed several Parliamentary Questions (PQs) regarding the recent spate of layoffs worldwide by tech firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: News sources have reported global retrenchment numbers at more than 21,000 employees across close to 50 tech companies worldwide in November 2022 alone, more than any other month this year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, the impact of recent global tech layoffs on our local workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, the employment support measures for affected workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am taking these questions together to provide a more holistic response.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I will begin with an overview of employment trends in the tech sector, as well as the impact of recent global tech layoffs on our local workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: While there are no clearly defined boundaries, the tech sector generally refers to the Information and Communications (I&C) sector.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As of June 2022, the I&C sector employs 136,100 residents.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This number has increased steadily over the past five years, growing by an average of 8,100 resident workers per year from June 2017 to June 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In comparison, retrenchment numbers over the past five years have been relatively low, at an average of 790 resident workers per year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Melvin Yong and Ms He Ting Ru have also filed written questions asking about retrenchment in the sector in 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Based on the available labour market data, 260 residents were retrenched in the first half of this year, as compared to an increase of 7,000 residents employed in the sector.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Nonetheless, recent retrenchment notices received by MOM indicate an uptick in retrenchment of residents in the sector.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is consistent with the low median age of employed residents in the I&C sector.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Next, on employment support measures for affected workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Most workers from the I&C sector have been able to secure a job soon after retrenchment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the second quarter of 2022, the rate of re-entry into employment within six months post-retrenchment for residents in the sector was higher than for the overall economy, for both tech and non-tech workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This suggests that retrenched non-tech workers had also found employment opportunities across the I&C sector and the larger economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Dr Shahira Abdullah’s question on whether demand for tech talent has started to fall this year, job vacancies in the I&C sector have in fact continued to rise in the first half of this year, from 11,100 in December 2021 to 12,100 in June 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This latest figure is more than triple the 3,800 vacancies in June 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, other sectors like financial services, including local banks, are also hiring for tech roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Taken together, this reflects that there is strong absorptive capacity across the larger economy and opportunities for affected workers to fill in-demand roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Furthermore, half of the retrenching tech firms between July and mid-November 2022 have engaged outplacement partners or tapped on their industry networks to provide career transition services for their affected workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, the Taskforce for Responsible Retrenchment and Employment Facilitation (RTF), comprising representatives from Workforce Singapore (WSG) and NTUC’s Employment and Employability Institute (e2i), is reaching out to all affected local employees, including the youths which Dr Shahira Abdullah has asked about, to offer employment support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This includes information kits on job fairs, career advisory and coaching services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For retrenched non-tech workers, we will also encourage them to consider Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs) as well as skills upgrading to improve their chances of returning to the workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The RTF provides relevant information on CCPs during their engagements with retrenching firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: NTUC’s e2i also collaborated with Tech Talent Assembly, Accenture and Amazon Web Services to organise an Infocomm Jobs and Skills Fair in November 2022 providing some 400 jobs on offer.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, to Ms Joan Pereira’s question regarding tripartite partnership to support affected employees, it is already happening.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To ensure that affected workers receive timely and effective support, it is important that retrenching firms adhere to the requirement to submit notices of retrenchment to MOM within five working days of notifying affected employees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To answer Ms Joan Pereira's question on whether tech firms have been prompt in submitting notices of retrenchment to MOM, the majority of retrenchment notifications from the I&C sector since July 2022 were submitted on time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Employers who do not submit on time are issued with caution letters.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Looking ahead, Dr Lim Wee Kiak has asked if the Government expects more layoffs of tech employees in the next six months.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: MOM is mindful that hiring demand may moderate in some parts of the I&C sector given macro-economic uncertainties and risks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Employees who have been dismissed or retrenched may need assistance, but may feel that the HR of their company are not on their side due to various circumstances.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MOM be able to provide a channel or dedicated hotline for such employees to seek some advice as to what they can do and what options they have?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We would not hesitate to consider other means should the retrenchment numbers continue to rise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have also mentioned in my reply earlier on, besides the hotline, there are significant efforts done by the RTF to reach out to employees who are being retrenched.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of providing resources in the form of information kits on job fairs, career advisory and coaching services, the RTF also encourages retrenched non-tech workers to consider upgrading themselves through career conversion programmes (CCPs) and skills upgrading to improve their chances of returning to the workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on, that while the retrenchments are happening in tech firms, there is a proportionate difference in tech roles and non-tech roles within these tech companies as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Generally, the employees who are being retrenched in the tech roles have been able to find jobs much faster post-retrenchment compared to those in the non-tech roles, which takes a bit longer.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, the RTF is also focusing on helping retrenched employees in these non-tech roles to upgrade, to convert the skills, to pivot and to allow them a much better chance of getting employment.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I think he had not responded to the second part of my Parliamentary Question (PQ), which is whether this layoff will have a knock-on effect on the salary adjustment of workers in the tech industry.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The Minister pointed out just now, that a large majority who were laid off were actually in the non-tech domain.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As for the median salary of non-tech employees who have been retrenched, we do not have that data because retrenching firms are not required to include the salary data of retrenched employees when submitting Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications (MRNs) to the Ministry.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, I am unable to comment on the breakdown of the non-tech roles of these employees who are being retrenched and whether they will experience knock-on effects on salary adjustment later on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In November 2022 alone, we monitored the four big tech firms which the media had reported on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If I use that as a proxy, it is a bit early for us to comment on whether there will be knock-on effects for those in tech roles in the immediate term, given the huge number of vacancies vis-à-vis those looking for a job.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the non-tech roles, as I have shared earlier on, we are supporting them through the RTF and TAFEP, we are going through e2i and WSG to encourage this group to upgrade, reskill and also attend some career conversion programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the companies that have the ability to use NTUC's Company Training Committees, that is an added avenue for them to train and reskill their workers as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that answers part of your question.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is, I am mindful of the uncertain outlook that the IT sector is facing globally but may I ask the Minister about potential job opportunities in the future?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think Minister mentioned that the positions for tech is still abundant, but may I ask him about the private versus public tech opportunities?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because with the uncertain outlook, the private sector opportunities would probably be uncertain.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can Minister mention what type of skillsets and outlook would be needed for the young ones?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because we have been pushing for young people to go into the tech sector with the promotion of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and all that.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is in relation to my PQ.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think Minister has not answered the last part of my PQ, which is whether the Ministry will engage industry actors to centralise information to ensure fairer and more equitable re-employment processes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The ones in tech roles are about one-third of the total proportion being retrenched.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I also shared earlier on in my response to Miss Cheryl Chan's supplementary question that this group of people will find employment quite quickly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of working to help those in non-tech roles, we are also stepping up efforts to help them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The next few months are going to be quite critical, given the continued geopolitical uncertainties and also depending on whether the global supply chain disruptions continue.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we see that many of the areas that we have pivoted into and significantly invested in through our Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) as well as the Job Transformation Maps that run alongside them, such as the financial services sector, seem to be still moving ahead as growth sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we will do whatever we can to pivot those that would want to be pivoted, that would want to be transformed, into these sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the same time, for the business-to-consumer (B2C) tech firms, we are watching developments very closely.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, I could request for Mr Saktiandi Supaat to file another PQ in the first quarter of 2023 to see how successful our follow-up action has been.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I wanted to follow up on my PQ.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I think I did not hear the answer to the first part of my PQ, which is the portion on those impacted; how many of those are Singaporeans versus foreigners.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: My second supplementary question would be, I understand that there are still a lot of jobs available.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But, in the current climate where businesses are also relocating or looking at their location strategies, is the Minister concerned at this point, given the rise in tech sector salaries in the recent past, whether our competitiveness as a tech sector – in terms of cost and availability of manpower and the ability to fill these roles quickly – is in any way compromised?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The reason why we did not provide the level of granularity that she has asked for is that we typically do not break down resident data further into Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We follow a practice that is aligned with the official statistics set out by the International Labour Organization (ILO), as statistical agencies worldwide typically cover the population residing in their country when presenting statistical releases, without a breakdown by nationality.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, if I may provide an indication, citizens make up a large majority of our resident labour force, at about 85%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The PR population has also remained stable over time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, if you take it together, this means that the resident data mirrors citizen data.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And if we were to break it down, it provides little additional information.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To her separate point on the cost issue, we have taken a very curated and differentiated approach to upskill, to upgrade the skillsets of our entire workforce with a focus on the Singaporean Core as our principle.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There will obviously be some parts in the entire value chain, for which companies will want to take advantage of offshoring some services to capture some arbitrage opportunities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But I do not think this is always possible or easy for companies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I would humbly request that she files a separate PQ if she wants some level of granularity on offshoring, so that we can provide better statistics.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I think the big question is, of course, when they find jobs, are they equivalent jobs or are they of the same salary?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If MOM does not track at the point of time of the retrenchment, the salary, then I would like to ask MOM, why not?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Would MOM start tracking now, so we will roughly know what is the gap that they are facing?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And then, at least the Government can provide some assistance in this way, so that they can lessen or cushion the impact of retrenchment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have earlier on shared that, thus far in the I&C sector, the median income has been on an upward trajectory.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To go into the granularity for each type of non-tech role, I think would be very granular.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If this is what you are suggesting for us to track, it is something that we could look into, but we need to understand why.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we are very careful, in terms of making sure that our Singapore Core and our residents who are working here, continue to possess the skills and to keep ahead.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, this is the focus of what MOM will be looking at in the months ahead.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that that gives you some reassurance, that this is one aspect that we are singularly focused on.
